By Dean Bilton

By Simon Smale

Topic:Cricket

Australia looks to build on its spectacular first Test victory over South Africa when the series moves to Gqeberha in the Eastern Cape.

Follow all the action from St George's in our live blog below, keep up to date with all the latest stats in our ScoreCentre, and tune in to our live radio coverage.

By Simon Smale

By Simon Smale

I don't wish to be premature, but I feel like it's time to call it.

By Simon Smale

Any update on the weather???

- Ashley Schaffer

And there have been no checks from the umpires - for the aforementioned reason.

There is still time left in the day before they call it, but I am not overly hopeful.

By Simon Smale

There's nothing I like better than a classic cricket ground, and St George's Park definitely fits that bill.

St George's Park is the oldest Test venue in South Africa, hosting the 31st Test in history back in March 1889.

It was the first Test to ever be held outside of Australia or England and just the seventh Test venue ever used after the MCG, The Oval, Lord's, SCG, Adelaide Oval and Old Trafford.

England won that first Test by 8 wickets, the match finishing inside two days.

England were the first four opponents to play at the ground, and won all of those matches, which were played in 1896, 1914 and 1949.

Australia played there for the first time in 1950 and won by an innings and 259 runs, Arthur Morris (157), Neil Harvey (116) and Lindsay Hassett (167) all scoring big in their first innings total of 7-549 declared.

Keith Miller than took 4-42 to help bowl the South Africans out for 158, before they were bowled out again following on for 132.

South Africa won their first match at the ground in 1954, beating New Zealand by 5 wickets and, in 1957, beat England there for the first time by 58 runs.

The lowest team total ever scored at the ground was 30 all out by South Africa against England in 1896, with the next lowest coming much more recently, Zimbabwe bowled out for just 68 in 30.1 overs in 2017, and Bangladesh falling for 80 in 2022.

Herschelle Gibbs' 196 against India in 2001 is the highest ever score at the venue, while Keshav Maharaj possesses the best innings figures of any bowler in recent years with a 7-40 against Bangladesh in 2022.

By Simon Smale

Am I the only one who's had fourteen snacks and twenty-seven coffees during these 12.2 overs ? Anymore rain and I'll burst !

- Old timer

I have already noted to Dean that rain delays are incredibly dangerous for the amount of food that I eat during them.

We are approaching a critical moment, I think...

By Simon Smale

.... I think the St George's sousaphone needs draining though. Make a cracking rain gauge.

- Old timer

Might be good to capture the rain, but I wonder whether they will be able to read the values without emptying it.

Plus the water would play havoc with the cork pads.

By Simon Smale

No, not the cricketers, these players.

Key Event

By Simon Smale

The players have taken tea, so there will be nothing doing til at least half past the hour.

But it seems like a good tea to  take, because it's still raining.

By Simon Smale

Is the 13th over a little early for the St George’s Park brass band to blow their own trumpets?

- Mike

I, for one, applaud their spirit.

Much like the band that played as the Titanic sunk beneath the waves, staying positive and keeping spirits high as one's feet get damp is essential.

By Simon Smale

This Test will be particularly interesting watching as an Englishman - conditions here seem quite similar to what may come up in the Ashes next year if the previous English summer is anything to go by!

- Josh

By Simon Smale

I'll go first - Scotty Boland, 'The Sensational One'

- Mike

I think I'm feeling the Mordialloc Maestro more to be honest.

But seeing as cricket looks about as far away as it's been all day, let's open it up to the floor....

By Simon Smale

He's not an official member of CLASH but Scotty Boland probably would be in just about every other Test team.

As Ric Finlay notes, Boland's start in Test cricket can be considered among the very best of anyone in terms of wickets taken.

He is only 10 wickets behind Captain Pat at the same stage of his career.

Makes you feel sorry for him to an extent - a man born in the wrong era given the stability and longevity of those ahead of him in the pecking order.

By Dean Bilton

Dean, this may have been said already, but would you consider changing your surname to Biltong for the remainder of this tour?

- Mark Butcher

It is not been the first time this has been asked of me tonight. But yes, in the name of maintaining good relations between the two countries throughout this series I can indeed make that sacrifice.

By Simon Smale

By Dean Bilton

Not really. Still raining, big covers still on, no real sign of any progress at the minute.

There are still technically three and a half hours from which we could get some more cricket tonight, and so we continue to wait.

By Dean Bilton

By Dean Bilton

Were going to tell our grandkids the legend of Boland and they just won't believe us that he only played like 3 tests a year.

- LW

On a similar note for the longest time, I always thought young Patrick Cummins was going to be the great random old man story of our generation. Back when his injuries kept him from playing and he only had that one Test to his name.

"Let me tell you the tale of a boy called Cummins. Or maybe it was Cummings, nobody really knows for sure. They say he played just one game in South Africa as a wee lad, either 13 or 18 years old, depending on who you ask. It doesn't matter. He bowled liked the wind, faster than Thommo but on Lillee's line and length. He took a million wickets, he hit the winning runs, he won man of the match... and then he disappeared. Never to be seen again. They say Jacques Kallis still sees his baby face in his nightmares."

Anyway yeah, Scott Boland's good. And it's raining again.

By Dean Bilton

This really is the worst sort of weather for cricket. The on and off really does make for the worst days, especially for a batting side who are on a hiding to nothing.

It looks moderately heavy now and the big covers are coming out. Time to once again play the waiting game.

By Dean Bilton

He may well bowl all day from this end, the way he's going. The only thing that may stop him is the weather, and the ground staff are poised by the fence in case they get the call.

BEATEN! Bavuma's outside edge is again beaten.

Aaaaand the umpire's are taking them off again. Fun while it lasted.

By Dean Bilton

For the first time today, the Aussie skipper is going to have a bowl. Cummins running in at Ackerman now.

Cummins drops in a short one and Ackerman hooks it fine, only for two runs. Looks like it actually took the glove, beating Ackerman for pace.

In other, less positive news it does seem to be drizzling again. Let's hope it remains at a light drizzle.

Two from the over, solid stuff from Ackerman.
